derivations.claim: Regard a matrix as its finite list of real coordinates. Multiplying the independent scalar densities in [F1] gives joint density $C e^{-\|G\|_F^2/2}$ over $\mathbb R$ or $C'e^{-\|G\|_F^2}$ over $\mathbb C$. The maps $G\mapsto U^*GV$ are real-linear isometries for the Frobenius norm; their real Jacobian matrix $O$ satisfies $O^TO=I$, hence $|\det O|=1$. Apply the invariance with $U=W$ and $V=I$. Disjoint coordinate blocks of the resulting iid matrix have a joint density that factors into the product of their block densities, which is exactly independence; both blocks have their declared standard laws.

index $i$, $((GG^*)^{-1})_{ii}$ has distribution $1/U$ with
